method: typology of political resistance; 30 interviews + 50 press articles
definition: No PG definition - energy-transition governance & local political agency in a multi-level (unitary French) system (p. 1).
stakeholders: Local elected officials as political mediators who 'interpret, mediate, and sometimes amplify' opposition (p. 6).
temporality_detail: Core & explicitly electoral (keystone). NIMEY; 'electoral mandates are short-lived. This temporal misalignment reinforces both NIMEY and NIMTOO behaviours' (p. 6).
megaproject_detail: Inter-org/multi-level core; large infrastructure, not $1bn megaproject.
misalignment_detail: Empirical instantiation of the RQ's mechanism for local officials & renewable-energy projects. Remaining gap: scale to megaproject governance with multiple electoral turnovers per project.
gaps: Names the exact mechanism (electoral misalignment) but at local-official / non-megaproject scale.
key_quotes: 'The benefits of energy transition programmes generally materialise in the medium to long term, whereas electoral mandates are short-lived. This temporal misalignment reinforces both NIMEY and NIMTOO behaviours' (p. 6).
Local officials 'interpret, mediate, and sometimes amplify' opposition (p. 6).
coding_notes: The single closest template (NIMEY/NIMTOO) to the thesis's construct; built for local politics, to be scaled up.
